newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber mixed on start of new trading year.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber mixed on start of new trading year.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed mixed on the first trading day of 1997, with most players either holidaying and absent from active market participation.
The closure of the Singapore market for national elections also meant fewer leads for players to follow, said traders.
"It's been a real quiet day and I don't think anything's going to change tomorrow," said a trader.
"I think some serious involvement will only be seen next week," said another trader. "Most players are still in holiday mood and there's just two more days to end this week."

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted February RSS1 buyer at 315.50 cents ($1.25) a kg, down half cent from Tuesday. February SMR20 was priced two cents higher at 312 cents a kg.
Dealers said they expected prices to remain steady in the coming week as supply of raw materials have tightened after seasonal rains reduced rubber tapping at plantations.
The INRO five-day average was 241.71 Malaysian/Singapore cents (96 cents) per kg on Dec 31 from 241.57 on Dec 30. The daily indicator was 241.98 against 241.80 previously.
